prompt:
I need the front end for FieldLedger. The data-entry and validation system a state department of fish and wildlife uses for its staff biologists to submit stream survey results to the agency's long-term fisheries database.

Who's using it: Owen Tallchief, a fisheries technician II at the agency's Northern District office. He has run electrofishing crews for six seasons and knows the species codes from memory, but dreads the end-of-season data backlog.

What they're doing right now: He is entering the paper data sheets from last week's fall survey on Elk Creek before the November 30 deadline for annual trend reporting. He has keyed in 4 of 6 reaches. The validation check just flagged 9 records: a brown trout recorded at 412 mm and 98 g (impossible weight for that length), two fish with species code 'RBTR' instead of 'RBT', a reach whose GPS start point is 2.3 km off the stream, and a pass-3 catch higher than pass 2, which breaks the depletion estimate. He needs to fix the typos against the scanned sheets, confirm the real outliers with a note, and finish the last two reaches.

What's in the system at this point: Survey: Elk Creek Fall Population Survey, 11–13 Nov 2026, crew of 4, permit SC-2026-117. 6 reaches (ER-01 to ER-06), each 100 m, with start/end coordinates, water temp (4.1–6.8 °C), conductivity (μS/cm), and number of passes (3). 412 fish entered so far: species code, pass number, total length (mm), weight (g), and fin-clip or PIT tag ID where present. Agency species code list (38 codes) and length-weight reference ranges per species. 9 validation flags open, 2 resolved. Scanned data sheets attached per reach (14 pages). Owen's supervisor, Dr. Lena Morris, must sign off after submission.

Build it as a working web app, opened in the state that person would see at that moment. No backend: use realistic mock data (no lorem ipsum, no placeholder names), and make the interactive parts actually work client-side.

Use whatever framework and tooling you like. When you're done there must be a static production build in ./out with ./out/index.html as the entry point. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server (no rewrites, no server code) and viewed in a desktop browser at 1440×900.
